title: DeepSeek History: From High-Flyer to V4.1 Flash (2026)
summary: DeepSeek history from 2023 to 2026: Liang Wenfeng and High-Flyer, the R1 shock that hit Nvidia, MIT-licensed open weights, V4 Pro, V4.1 Flash, and funding.
body_markdown:
DeepSeek is the Hangzhou lab that made frontier AI cheap. In under three years it went from a side project inside a quant hedge fund to **DeepSeek-R1** , the open-weight reasoning model that knocked close to $600 billion off Nvidia's market value in a single day, and then to the **V4** family that runs a 1-million-token context window under the MIT license.


How did a team that never raised outside money until 2026 change the price of intelligence for everyone? Who is Liang Wenfeng? And what changed between V3, R1, V4 Pro, and V4.1 Flash? This is the full DeepSeek story, updated for October 2026.


> **TL;DR:** DeepSeek was spun out of the High-Flyer hedge fund on **July 17, 2023** . **V2** (May 2024) started a price war, **R1** (January 2025) shocked markets, and the **V4** family (2026) brought MIT-licensed models with a **1-million-token** context. DeepSeek V4 Pro is in the[Taskade model picker](https://www.taskade.com/docs/models/deepseek) on every paid plan.[Build an app with it →](https://www.taskade.com/create?entry_kind=content&source=blog&entry=%2Fblog%2Fdeepseek-ai-history)


The[TSK-1 Benchmark](https://www.taskade.com/tsk) sends the same app request to each model family and records what got built. The[DeepSeek results](https://www.taskade.com/tsk/deepseek) show how DeepSeek models do on real app builds.


## What Is DeepSeek?


DeepSeek is a Chinese AI company headquartered in Hangzhou, Zhejiang, that builds large language models and releases most of them as open weights under the MIT license. It was founded on July 17, 2023 as a spin-out of the quantitative hedge fund High-Flyer, and it is led by its founder, Liang Wenfeng.


DeepSeek is unusual among frontier labs in three ways. It funded itself from a trading firm's profits for its first three years. It published detailed technical reports on how it trained its models, cost figures included. And it priced its API so low that rivals in China and the US had to cut their own prices to keep up.

## Who Founded DeepSeek? Meet Liang Wenfeng


Liang Wenfeng is a Chinese engineer and investor who studied electronic and information engineering at Zhejiang University. In 2015 he co-founded High-Flyer, a quantitative hedge fund that used machine learning to trade, and he grew it into one of China's largest quant funds.


High-Flyer built its own GPU clusters for trading research, named Fire-Flyer. Reports say Liang bought about 10,000 Nvidia A100 GPUs in 2021, before US export rules restricted those chips in China. That stockpile, and the engineering habits of a trading firm, shaped everything DeepSeek did next.


Liang has said in interviews that DeepSeek's goal is research toward artificial general intelligence, not quick revenue. The company hires mostly young researchers from Chinese universities, keeps a small team (reported at under 200 people in 2025), and publishes its methods.


## How Did DeepSeek Start Inside a Hedge Fund?


DeepSeek started as an AI research lab that High-Flyer announced on April 14, 2023, and spun out as a separate company on July 17, 2023. High-Flyer stayed the principal investor and funded the lab from its trading profits. Liang held a majority stake through holding companies.


That funding model mattered. With no venture investors to answer to, DeepSeek could spend its first years on research papers and open releases instead of a consumer product. The lab's first models were small and technical. Each one introduced a method that the next model built on.


## Every DeepSeek Model Explained (2023 to 2026)


DeepSeek released more than 15 models in three years. The table below lists the releases that changed the lab's direction. Dates are DeepSeek's own release dates.

### DeepSeek Coder and LLM 67B (2023): The Quiet Start


DeepSeek's first public models were DeepSeek Coder in November 2023 and DeepSeek LLM 67B later that month. Both were dense transformer models in the style of Meta's Llama. They were competitive with other open models of the time, but they were not the reason anyone outside China learned the name.


### DeepSeek-V2 (May 2024): The Price War


DeepSeek-V2 combined two ideas that defined the lab. The first was a mixture-of-experts design with 236 billion total parameters and only about 21 billion active per token. The second was **multi-head latent attention (MLA)** , which compresses the memory a model keeps while it reads a long prompt.


Together they made V2 very cheap to serve, and DeepSeek priced its API at about 1 yuan per million input tokens. Within weeks, ByteDance, Alibaba, Baidu, and Tencent cut their own prices. Chinese media called it a price war, and DeepSeek started it.


### DeepSeek-V3 (December 2024): Frontier Weights for Everyone


DeepSeek-V3, released on December 26, 2024, has 671 billion total parameters, of which about 37 billion are active for each token. DeepSeek trained it on 14.8 trillion tokens and reported that the final training run took about 2.79 million H800 GPU hours.


That GPU-hour figure, priced at $2 per hour, became the famous "$5.6 million" training cost. The number was real, but narrow. It covered only the last training run and left out research, failed runs, data work, salaries, and the hardware itself. Even so, it showed that a frontier-class model did not need a nine-figure training run.


### DeepSeek-R1 (January 2025): The Reasoning Shock


DeepSeek-R1, released on January 20, 2025, is a reasoning model that thinks step by step before it answers, in the style of OpenAI's o1. DeepSeek trained it on top of V3 with large-scale reinforcement learning, and it published a sibling, **R1-Zero** , that learned to reason from reinforcement learning alone.


Three things made R1 different from earlier reasoning models:


- **It was MIT-licensed.** Anyone could download it, run it, and build on it.
- **It showed its reasoning.** The chat app printed the model's full chain of thought.
- **It came with small distilled versions** built on Qwen and Llama, so a laptop could run a reasoning model.


To learn how reasoning models think, read[AI reasoning models explained](https://www.taskade.com/blog/reasoning-models) .


### DeepSeek V3.1 to V3.2 (2025): One Model, Two Modes


Through 2025 DeepSeek merged its chat and reasoning lines. V3.1 (August 2025) let one model switch between a thinking mode and a fast mode. V3.2-Exp (September 2025) introduced DeepSeek Sparse Attention, which reads only the parts of a long context that matter for each token, and DeepSeek cut API prices by more than half the same day. V3.2 shipped as a stable model on December 1, 2025.


### DeepSeek V4 Pro and V4 Flash (2026): A Million Tokens


DeepSeek released the V4 family as a preview on April 24, 2026, after reports had pointed to an earlier launch in February. **V4 Pro** has 1.6 trillion total parameters and about 49 billion active per token. **V4 Flash** is a smaller 284-billion-parameter model. Both carry a 1-million-token context window and the MIT license.


V4 Flash reached its official release on July 31, 2026, and V4 Pro left preview on August 13, 2026. To see how context windows grew this large, read the[history of the context window](https://www.taskade.com/blog/context-window-history) .


### DeepSeek V4.1 Flash (September 2026): A New Architecture


DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, released on September 10, 2026, is the first and smallest model of a new DeepSeek architecture family. DeepSeek says the new architecture is built for a higher capability ceiling, faster inference, and higher throughput, and the model has native multimodal visual understanding. DeepSeek also lowered its API prices with the release.


## Why Did DeepSeek R1 Shock the Stock Market?


DeepSeek R1 shocked the stock market because it suggested that frontier reasoning could be built and served with far fewer chips than investors had priced in. On January 27, 2025, a week after the R1 launch, DeepSeek's free app passed ChatGPT as the most downloaded free app on the US App Store.


That day Nvidia shares fell about 17 percent, a loss of close to $600 billion in market value and the largest one-day loss for any US company at the time. Other chip and power stocks fell with it. The fear was simple. If a lab with export-restricted GPUs could match the frontier at a fraction of the cost, the race to build ever-larger data centers might be overbuilt.


The fear faded within months. Cheaper models led to more AI use, not less, and chip demand kept climbing. Economists pointed to the Jevons paradox: when a resource gets cheaper, total use often goes up. For the hardware side of this story, read[the history of Nvidia and Jensen Huang](https://www.taskade.com/blog/nvidia-jensen-history) and[how AI data centers work](https://www.taskade.com/blog/ai-data-centers-explained) .


## How Does DeepSeek's Architecture Work?


DeepSeek's architecture rests on two ideas: send each token to a few specialist experts, and compress the memory the model keeps about the prompt. Both cut the compute and memory each answer needs, which is how DeepSeek keeps its prices low.


Technique First used in What it does in plain English


Mixture of experts DeepSeekMoE, V2 Runs only a few expert sub-networks per token, so a huge model costs like a small one


Multi-head latent attention V2 Shrinks the memory kept for each token of the prompt, so long inputs fit


GRPO DeepSeekMath, R1 A cheaper reinforcement learning method that scores groups of answers against each other


Multi-token prediction V3 Trains the model to predict several tokens ahead, which speeds learning


DeepSeek Sparse Attention V3.2-Exp Reads only the parts of a long context that matter for each token


If the transformer basics are new to you, start with[how large language models work](https://www.taskade.com/blog/how-do-llms-work) .


## Is DeepSeek Open Source? The MIT License Explained


Most current DeepSeek models are open-weight under the MIT license. MIT is one of the most permissive licenses in software. It allows commercial use, modification, and redistribution, with no revenue threshold and no attribution banner in your product.


DeepSeek-R1 used MIT from its launch in January 2025, and the V4 family kept it in 2026. Earlier models used a custom DeepSeek model license with use restrictions. The training data and the full training pipeline are not released, so "open weight" is the more precise term. For the wider story, read[the history of open-source LLMs](https://www.taskade.com/blog/open-source-llm-history) and our guide to[the best open-source LLMs](https://www.taskade.com/blog/open-source-llms) .


## How Did DeepSeek Get Funded?


DeepSeek ran on High-Flyer's money until 2026. In June 2026 it closed its first outside funding round, reported at about 50 billion yuan (roughly $7.4 billion), at a valuation reported above $50 billion. Tencent and battery maker CATL were reported among the largest outside investors. Liang Wenfeng also invested his own money, and the deal kept him in control.


In October 2026, reports said DeepSeek was in talks for a larger second round and was preparing for a possible stock listing as early as 2027. Valuations in AI move fast, so treat any single figure as a dated snapshot.

## Controversies and Open Questions


DeepSeek's rise came with scrutiny, and an honest history includes it.


- **Data and privacy.** The DeepSeek app and API run on servers in China. Italy's privacy regulator blocked the app in January 2025, Australia ordered it off government devices in February 2025, and the US defense budget law for 2026 restricts it on defense devices.
- **Distillation claims.** OpenAI said in 2025, and Anthropic said in February 2026, that they saw signs of their models' outputs being used to train other labs' models, DeepSeek included.
- **The real cost.** The "$5.6 million" V3 figure is often quoted as the full cost of the model. It is not. It is the GPU rental value of one final training run.


The open-weight license is the practical answer to the first point. A company that cannot send data to DeepSeek's servers can run the same model on its own infrastructure. A team that wants these models without servers or code can start from[no-code AI builders that run open-weight models](https://www.taskade.com/blog/open-model-builders) .

## What's Next for DeepSeek?


DeepSeek's next steps point in three directions. A V4.1 Pro model would complete the new architecture family that V4.1 Flash started. Fresh funding gives the lab more compute than High-Flyer alone could buy. And the open-weight releases keep pushing the price of intelligence down for everyone who builds on top of models.


For builders, the lesson of DeepSeek is that the model layer keeps getting cheaper and better, and it changes every few months. ## Frequently Asked Questions About DeepSeek


What is DeepSeek?


DeepSeek is a Chinese artificial intelligence company based in Hangzhou that builds large language models and releases most of them as open weights under the MIT license. It was spun out of the quantitative hedge fund High-Flyer in July 2023 and is led by founder and CEO Liang Wenfeng. Its best-known models are DeepSeek-R1, released in January 2025, and the DeepSeek V4 family released in 2026.


Who founded DeepSeek?


DeepSeek was founded by Liang Wenfeng, who co-founded the High-Flyer quantitative hedge fund in 2015. High-Flyer announced an artificial general intelligence research lab in April 2023 and spun it out as DeepSeek on July 17, 2023. High-Flyer funded the lab for its first three years, and Liang kept control of the company through its first outside funding round in 2026.


Why did DeepSeek R1 crash Nvidia stock?


On January 27, 2025, a week after DeepSeek released R1, its free chatbot app passed ChatGPT as the most downloaded free app on the US App Store. Investors concluded that frontier reasoning might need far fewer chips than assumed, and Nvidia shares fell about 17 percent in one session, a loss of close to $600 billion in market value. It was the largest one-day loss for any US company at the time.


How much did it cost to train DeepSeek V3?


DeepSeek reported that the final training run of DeepSeek V3 used about 2.79 million H800 GPU hours, which it valued at about $5.6 million at a rental price of $2 per GPU hour. The figure covers only that final run. It excludes research, failed experiments, data work, salaries, and the cost of owning the hardware, so the full cost of building V3 was much higher.


Is DeepSeek open source?


Most DeepSeek models ship as open weights under the MIT license, which lets anyone download, run, modify, and sell products built on the model. DeepSeek-R1 used the MIT license from launch in January 2025, and the V4 family kept it in 2026. The training data and full training code are not released, so open weight is the more precise term than open source.


What is the difference between DeepSeek V4 Pro and V4.1 Flash?


DeepSeek V4 Pro is the large model of the V4 family, with 1.6 trillion total parameters, a 1-million-token context window, and a focus on deep reasoning and coding. DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, released on September 10, 2026, is the smallest model of a new DeepSeek architecture family and adds native image understanding. Flash is built for speed and low cost, and Pro is built for depth.


What is a mixture-of-experts model?


A mixture-of-experts model splits its parameters into many smaller expert networks and uses a router to send each token to only a few of them. DeepSeek V3 has 671 billion parameters in total but activates about 37 billion per token, so it runs at the cost of a much smaller model. Every DeepSeek flagship since V2 uses this design.


Is DeepSeek safe to use for business?


The answer depends on how you run it. The DeepSeek chat app and API run on DeepSeek's own servers in China, and several governments restricted them on official devices in 2025. Because the weights are MIT-licensed, a company can also run DeepSeek models on its own infrastructure or through a provider it already trusts, which keeps data inside its own controls.
